great_tartary_plains: The horizon refuses to settle. Aether moves under the grass like breath under a sheet.
Compasses turn here as if remembering an older north.
This is the wound itself. Centuries have not closed it.
Storms of violet and blue argue overhead in a tongue no one alive still speaks.
The plains keep the cataclysm fresh, the way mud keeps a footprint.
Time runs uneven here. A long stride may cost an hour. A short one may cost a year.
Walk softly. The ground above the buried cities is thin in places, and listening.
The wind here carries names. Most of them belong to nobody alive.
Old roads thread the grass, paved with stone that does not erode. The roads do not lead where they used to.
Reclaimers cross these plains in long quiet lines. They do not speak. The plains punish noise.
asgardar: The capital sleeps under Aetherstone, breathing through cracks no shovel can widen.
Once, the Grand Spire poured the heavens into these streets. The streets are still bright in places no light reaches.
Mud Monarch heralds still walk these avenues, though the avenues are buried and the heralds long dead.
Asgardar does not forget being a capital. It only forgets that the world above has moved on.
Listen at the right wall and the city grid still hums, faint as a heart through a closed door.
The Giants planned for everything except being remembered like this.
Coins of the old mint surface in the rubble. They are still warm.
Banners hang in chambers no one has unsealed. They are the right colours.
Aether circles Asgardar like a watcher who has not decided whether to enter.
The capital is patient. It outwaited an empire. It will outwait you.
grand_spire_of_etheria: The Spire still drinks. From what celestial well, no one will answer.
Stand near its base and the Aether tightens around the chest, polite and proprietary.
Light moves up the inside of the tower in slow tides. It has its own schedule.
This was the throat of an empire. It is not entirely silent.
The Aetherborn feel the Spire before they see it. Some weep without knowing why.
Whatever the Spire was built to ground, it grounds it still.
Birds detour around the Spire's air column. The detour is wide. The birds are wise.
A single stone removed from the Spire weighs more in the hand than it did in the wall.
The Spire's shadow falls in the wrong direction at noon. No one comments on this anymore.
Climb the Spire only with intent. The Spire grades intent at every landing.
It drank the sun by day and the cold black sky by night, and gave the heat it could not use back to the stars. The radiators are dark now. The heat had to go somewhere.
samarran: The research city. The hum here is not metaphor.
Samarran does not rest. The walls are still working on Zalmar's last problem.
The mud arrived first to the laboratories. It learned things on the way in.
Diagrams ghost across the stone when the light is wrong. They redraw themselves if watched.
Every street here was a paper. The flood was the eraser. Some paragraphs survived.
Aetherons move thicker through Samarran's air. Lungs notice before minds do.
Glass vessels rest unbroken in the rubble. Some of them are still warm to the touch.
The university bell rings once a year, at no hour anyone has thought to record.
Scholars from the Order pilgrimage here. They do not all come back, but the ones who do come back changed.
An equation chalked on a wall here is older than every living language and still legible.
thametans_tower: The Engine is still in there. So is its mistake.
The walls hum at the frequency of the cascade. After a while, your bones learn the note.
Zalmar's last breath did not leave this tower. Few breaths do.
Touch nothing without need. Need will arrive uninvited.
This is where Tartaria asked the Aether for too much. The Aether has not finished answering.
Time pools on the upper floors. A minute spent there is rarely a minute when you leave.
The Aetheric Engine sleeps the way wounded animals sleep, with one eye open.
Brass valves on the lower levels turn themselves a quarter inch every century. Someone is counting.
Notes in Zalmar's hand are still pinned to the doors. The ink has not faded. The advice still applies.
Stairwells here loop in ways stairwells should not. Mark your steps.
The seals that fed the tower's heat to the sky cracked here first. You can still find the frost-line on the radiators where the cold stopped coming and the world caught fire instead.
voronov: Voronov was struck deepest. The flood found it on an ordinary morning.
Caches lie beneath this scar, intact, waiting for the right hand or the wrong one.
Houses here are whole, in their fashion, only inverted into the mud.
Reclaimers love Voronov. Voronov is patient with them, until it is not.
Aetherstone here is thinner in places. A pickaxe might break through. A foot certainly will.
The city kept its layout under the mud. Walk Voronov above-ground and you walk it below as well.
Lanterns in the lower city still flicker when the mud shifts. No one is lighting them.
Voronov's bell tower is upside down and ringing rarely. The bell is intact.
Children's toys surface here more often than coins. The mud is a strange editor.
Walk near the canals and the mud thins to slick clear water. Do not look down for long.
nimari: Half-swallowed. The half that remains has stopped pretending it is whole.
The Red Tower watches the plains. Faction banners change at its foot. The Tower does not.
Nimari's upper streets still hold roofs, doors, the suggestion of windows. Below, the mud is decisive.
Aetheric Cores hum at frequencies the body mistakes for hunger. Notice when you are not actually hungry.
The Mud Monarchs were born here, as much as they were born anywhere.
Listen for the bells. Nimari had bells, once. They sometimes remember.
Faction agents pass each other in Nimari's plazas without acknowledging the other exists. It is a small etiquette.
The cracked statues here still bleed Aether when the storms come close.
Doors in Nimari open inward, even the ones built to open out. The mud rewrote them.
Half a city is more than enough city for what walks here now.
red_tower_of_nimari: Red because of what the Aether did to its stone. Not because of paint.
A Core still beats in this tower. Every faction can hear it. So can you.
Climb only as high as your purpose. The Tower measures intent at each landing.
Sentinels patrol the inner stair, when they remember they are patrolling.
The light inside the Red Tower has weight. Stand under it long enough and you will feel it.
Many have reached the Core chamber. Few have left it the same.
Bloodlines older than the mud still match the Tower's locks. Newer hands meet older bolts.
The Tower's windows do not face outward. They face inward, into rooms that should not exist.
Aether condenses on the upper landings into thin red dew. It evaporates if breathed on.
Faction banners are tied at the Tower's foot every season. The Tower lets them rot in its own time.
varakush: The Forgotten Order keeps a door open here for those who know how to knock.
Lamps burn steady in Varakush. Steady lamps are rare in Tartaria. Notice them.
The library is older than the stronghold. The stronghold was built to protect the library.
Voices stay low here, not from fear, but from habit. Knowledge dislikes noise.
Rest is permitted. The Order's patience is finite, but it is genuine.
Tea, here, is a small ritual against the Aether. Drink the tea.
Scrolls in the deeper stacks reorder themselves when the moon is low. The librarians have stopped objecting.
Apprentices walk in pairs and write everything down. The Order remembers what gets written.
The kitchen here serves bread that does not stale. The recipe is not for the asking.
Varakush is one of the few places in Tartaria where the floor is reliably flat.
drakova: A Lost Capital. Lost means sealed, not destroyed. There is a difference.
Drakova waits the way old contracts wait: precisely, and with interest accruing.
The Aetherstone over Drakova is denser than the rest. Whatever is below was worth burying twice.
Some say a Core sleeps intact under Drakova. Some say it dreams.
The runes on the outermost stones have not weathered. The weather does not bother them.
Stand quietly. Drakova answers questions you have not yet thought to ask.
The Mud Monarchs were forbidden from Drakova by an older treaty than they admit to. They observe it.
Lamps here will not light. The dark is policy.
Drakova's gates are intact. They have not been opened since the mud arrived. They are not locked.
Walk Drakova's perimeter and your shadow walks a step behind, not below. Look once and then stop looking.
obsidian_pillars: The Pillars hate machines. Bring nothing that ticks if you mean to leave with it.
Black, polished, magnetic. They were aimed at something in the sky.
The observatory beneath the Pillars charted skies that no longer exist as charted.
Walk between two Pillars and your compass forgets you for a moment. Sometimes a long moment.
Birds will not perch here. Birds are wise.
The Pillars hum when the Aether storms come. They are the first to know.
Touch a Pillar with a bare hand and you will hear your own name in a voice you do not know.
The Pillars throw no shadow at noon. They throw two at dawn.
Aether collects in the basin between them like meltwater. It is not water. Do not drink.
Old maps marked the Pillars with a star. Old maps were not being polite.
endless_stair: Down, and down, and then a layer that refuses descent.
The Stair was built to be walked. It was not built to be reached.
Each step has been counted by someone. None of them agree on the number.
Aetheric pressure builds with depth. Past a certain landing, breath becomes a decision.
What is at the bottom is, in some sense, also at the top. The Stair confuses such distinctions.
Many have begun the descent. The Stair does not keep records, and neither does the mud below.
The Stair's walls are warm at the lower turns. Something below them is alive enough to give off heat.
Voices echo upward more easily than downward here. Speak quietly. Be heard quieter still.
Some steps have been worn smooth by feet. Others have not been stepped on by anything at all.
The lamps in the Stair are not lit by lamplighters. They light when needed. They are needed less often than you would think.
zharaks_teeth: Spires like a jawbone in shallow water. The water is shallow only at first.
Beautiful, by Tartarian standards. That has always been a warning.
Mud sirens nest in the highest spires. Their song is older than language and uses it anyway.
Do not answer what you hear here. Answers are how the Teeth feed.
The architecture rewards a quiet eye. The mud rewards a quiet foot.
At low tide, the Teeth show a little more. They never show all of themselves.
Boats wrecked on the Teeth do not surface. The Teeth do not return what they accept.
Aether storms gather here as if drawn by the architecture itself.
Each spire is hollow. Each spire is full. Both are true at different hours.
The Teeth were named by someone who survived them long enough to name them. That person did not return a second time.
sinking_cathedral: Only the steeple remains above the mud, and the steeple is leaning toward the listener.
The Cathedral keeps an artifact. The artifact keeps the Cathedral.
No one has returned. This is the cleanest statistic in Tartaria.
Bells should not still ring under mud. These do, occasionally, at no hour in particular.
Enter only if you have made peace with the possibility of staying.
The doors are open. The doors have always been open. That is the trap.
The pews below the mud are arranged for a service that has not adjourned.
Stained glass survives here in places it should not. The light through it falls on no one.
The Cathedral's clock has no hands. The clock keeps time anyway.
Faction priests of every banner refuse to bless this place. They do not refuse to acknowledge it.
cradle_of_dusk: The sky here is bruised with old Aether. It glows at hours that are not dusk.
Ships lie where the storms left them, crews intact, frozen mid-gesture.
Walk among the statues. Do not touch them. They were people, very recently in their own time.
The Cradle remembers the cascade as a single long moment, still happening.
Compass and clock will both surrender here. Bring patience instead.
What is dusk in the Cradle has been dusk for a long while. It is not waiting for night.
Aether lightning sketches itself across the air like a hand recalling a face.
Time pools here in basins. Step into one carefully and you may step out a different age.
The wind brings voices but never weather. Notice the difference.
Children's drawings, painted on stone, line the cliff walls. They are recent, by Cradle reckoning.
mud_seas: The Mud Seas are not sea, and not mud, and not still.
Currents move here without water moving. The Aether is the tide.
Whatever swims below was once something else. The mud was a long lesson.
Storms gather without sky. They arrive in the bones first.
Boats float here only by agreement. The agreement is renegotiated constantly.
A Leviathan's eye, kept dry, sees through these storms. Few keep such eyes.
The Mud Seas drown loud voices first. Yours, so far, has been careful.
Islands surface and submerge by Aether's whim. Maps are rewritten on the boats themselves.
Fish here have learned to walk, and most of them have forgotten how to swim.
The horizon does not flatten across the Mud Seas. It tilts. Notice when it tilts toward you.
giant_vault: The Giants lie here. Whether they sleep or are kept asleep is the question.
The Vault was sealed from the inside. That detail is rarely repeated.
Stand close to the door and the air tightens, as if a great chest were drawing breath.
The relics within outweigh kingdoms. The Giants within outweigh the relics.
Tartaria buried much. It locked very little. The Vault is one of the few.
If they wake, the question of who imprisoned whom will become urgent.
The True Tartarians do not approach the Vault. Their reverence does not require proximity.
Carvings on the Vault doors depict no events. They depict pauses between events.
Aether stops at the Vault's threshold as if asked politely.
The Vault's lock has no keyhole. It was never meant to be opened from outside.
mud_flood_nexus: This is the room where the disaster was managed, or could have been.
Touching the console here is not a small act. It is the act.
The Nexus has waited centuries to be addressed. It will answer.
Restoration and ruin sit on the same dial. The dial does not label them.
Every faction wants this room. The room has wanted, for some time, to be wanted differently.
Whatever happens here happens to Tartaria. Whatever happens to Tartaria happens to the world.
Decide slowly. The Aether keeps the minutes.
Brass levers here have been left in the position Zalmar last set them. No one has tried the second position.
The chamber's lighting follows the operator with quiet attention. It is not eager.
An inscription above the central console reads simply: not a wish.
etheric_chamber: The heart of it. The actual heart.
Automatons walk the Chamber's outer rings. They have not been relieved of their duty. They have not asked to be.
The traps here were designed by Tartarians at their cleverest. Their cleverest was considerable.
Aether sits thick in this air. Words slow. Thoughts slow. Both should be careful which way they finish.
The Chamber recognises a Tartarian bloodline. It is less courteous with strangers.
Light here is not lit. It is permitted.
Few have stood in this room with intact intent. Fewer have left with it.
The walls record what is said in this chamber. Whether the walls share what they record is its own question.
Each ring of the Chamber is colder than the last, and each ring is louder.
The Aetheric Chamber does not echo. It absorbs.
tartarian_outskirts: The borderlands. Where Tartaria thins, but does not stop.
Traps lie dormant in the grass, polite as sleeping dogs.
An expedition can die well here, and learn most of Tartaria's lessons in the process.
The Outskirts are kind to the careful and patient with the rest, briefly.
Aetheric anomalies pass through here on their way somewhere worse.
Markers, broken stones, half-buried signs. The Outskirts were once labeled.
Reclaimer caravans cut their own paths through these flats — no path holds for long.
A road here will end without warning, into mud or into Aether or into nothing at all.
Smoke columns rise on the horizon for hours and then are simply not there.
The Outskirts are where Tartaria practices being itself. The rehearsal is honest.
buried_cities: The buried cities sealed themselves under the same mud that killed them. There is no contradiction.
Time runs differently above each city. The map does not record this.
Aetherstone closed over these places like a verdict.
Below the seal, the streets are intact and the lamps are not entirely out.
Every buried city is a question Tartaria has not stopped asking.
Walk between cities and the air changes flavour. Each city was a different argument.
Excavation is not the only way in. Some doors are made of weather, or grief, or attention.
A buried city's name is heavier than the city itself. Speak names sparingly.
The seals are not all the same age. Some are still cooling.
Reclaimers have a saying: you do not unbury a city. You wait for it to remember itself.
